label: Started studying haemoglobin by X-ray crystallography
description: Perutz began his work on haemoglobin structure, considering it the most important unsolved problem in biochemistry.

sources.quote: I started to study haemoglobin by X-ray crystallography in 1937 because at that time the structure of proteins seemed the most important unsolved problem in biochemistry

label: 80th birthday celebration meeting at Royal Institution
description: A meeting in honour of Max Perutz titled 'Protein Crystallography and Medicine'.

sources.quote: His Medical Research Council colleagues duly organized a memorable meeting at the Royal Institution on 23 September 1994, 'Protein Crystallography and Medicine – a meeting in honour of Max Perutz'

label: Published prediction on structure-based drug discovery
description: Perutz wrote about the utility of enzyme structure in designing inhibitors.

sources.quote: Almost twenty years earlier he had written (Perutz, 1976) 'I started to study haemoglobin by X-ray crystallography in 1937...'

label: Contemplated averaging independent images as phasing tool
description: Bragg and Perutz seriously contemplated the use of averaging as a phasing tool.

sources.quote: first seriously contemplated as a phasing tool by Bragg and Perutz (Bragg & Perutz, 1952).

label: Published on protein crystallography with Bernal
description: Perutz co-authored a paper with Bernal and Fankuchen raising the use of averaging.

label: Moved to CSIRO
description: Colman moved to CSIRO, where he quoted Perutz to his masters.

sources.quote: When I moved to CSIRO in 1978 it was very convenient to quote Max Perutz to my masters.
